text: Attempt 16: attempt 15's dense start, plus the trip rule from the research: no factory-only districts; every factory cell next to homes; trips.py checks new land and the loop stops on weak trips.
Day one, dense (a15-day1).

Research after attempt 15 found why six attempts stopped near 20,000: the game only grows a lot after a random road trip of ~33 tiles reaches the right zone; our factory-only districts failed it (22-33% success). Attempt 16 mixes factories with homes everywhere.
Dense blocks 3 + 4 (a15-2003), coal #2 + pumps (a12-power1).
Tax controller: shops 4 -> 5 (demand 2000), factories 3 -> 4 (demand 2000)
Tax controller: shops 5 -> 6 (demand 2000), factories 4 -> 5 (demand 2000)
Coal #2 ($4,026, did not fit the cash with the dense blocks - same slip as attempt 15) and seaport + 19 north pumps ($6,046).

Control: the coal plant failed for lack of cash in the loan #2 build and I still started the clock (the run was gated on the audit only); power ran short within 7 months. From now on the clock starts only after every plan reports BUILD: checked.
Jul 2003: 6,140 people. The trip test passes everywhere: factory land 82% trip success (stalled land in earlier attempts: 22-33%).
Tax controller: shops 6 -> 7 (demand 2000), factories 5 -> 6 (demand 2000)
Loan #4 ($10,000): cash $127 after January; shop land short.
East block (shops + dense homes), east road link.
Tax controller: factories 6 -> 7 (demand 2000)
District 5 (mixed cells: factories next to homes, dense homes) without its gas plant: factory land short (16 empty, demand 2,000).
District 5 finished ($1,133), zoo ($3,016), coal plant (64,52) ahead of demand (district 5 went without its gas plant).
The gate worked: district 5's first build ran out of cash and the clock did not start until it was finished and checked.
